Full listing text could not be extracted (Dayforce candidate portal is JS-rendered), but the title's existence and active use by the employer is now confirmed by a first-party source rather than a single third-party job-aggregator snippet.

No ship named 'Kanawana' (or a close variant) has been found in any searched Furness Withy / Furness Bermuda Line fleet record: two independent fleet lists (GGA Archives' Furness Line list -- Digby, Dominica, Evangeline, Fort Amherst, Fort Townsend, Loyalist -- and the Furness Bermuda Line roster -- Bermudian/Fort Hamilton, Wandilla/Fort Victoria, Willochra/Fort St. George, Bermuda, Monarch of Bermuda, Queen of Bermuda), a general Wikipedia overview of the wider Furness Withy fleet (1,000+ ships across its history), and a full-text search of Lloyd's Register Foundation's digitized register collection on Internet Archive all returned zero matches. This does not rule out a ship of that name existing in an unindexed/undigitized register year or a smaller Furness subsidiary not covered by these sources, but the claim (from a 1951 primary source, that R.L. Charlton named the camp after a Furness Steamer) remains uncorroborated after this search.
The Order of Owens is an annual Camp Kanawana award presented to 'a Kanawanian who best exemplifies the leadership qualities and attitude of a canoe tripper at Camp Kanawana.'
The Order of Owens has been awarded annually from 1976 through 2026, except in 2020 and 2021 when it was not awarded because of the COVID-19 pandemic -- 49 award seasons in total.

The Order of Owens roster's first entry reads 'April 13, 1976 - Norrey Owens', carrying a full calendar date where all subsequent entries carry only a year, and bearing the name the award is called after. This wiki reads Norrey Owens as the award's namesake rather than its first recipient; the source does not state this and the reading is an inference.

Order of Owens recipients 1976-1999: 1976 Doug Peets; 1977 Denys Lawrence; 1978 Graham Scammells; 1979 Noelle Buck; 1980 Amy Pearce; 1981 Veronique Marin; 1982 Jean Perron; 1983 Gill Watt; 1984 Miriam Schleifer and Eric Boghen; 1985 Gesa Mahnke; 1986 Eyal Artzy; 1987 Mike Zeltzer; 1988 Aaron Chase; 1989 Siobhan Wallace; 1990 Shawna Silver; 1991 Simon Beauchemin; 1992 Susan Owen; 1993 Ryan Harbinson; 1994 Charles Leduc; 1995 Louis Lessard; 1996 Catherine Lalonde and Veronique Fraser; 1997 Francois Goulet-Lessard; 1998 Matthew Wiviott and Randall Blom; 1999 Theo Lerikos.

Order of Owens recipients 2000-2026: 2000 Mitchell McLarnon; 2001 Megan Robinson; 2002 Ian Braide; 2003 Julian Dobie; 2004 Alex Williams Zanis and Vienna Napier; 2005 Thomas Gilbert; 2006 Mike Romano; 2007 Meyland Gravel-Labelle; 2008 Oskar Newsam; 2009 Russel Donahue; 2010 Dylan Applebaum; 2011 Michael Sklivas; 2012 Emily Fleisler and Scott Bennet; 2013 Rosie Kaye; 2014 Pauline Morasse; 2015 Theo King; 2016 Owen Friesen; 2017 Louis Friedland-Yust; 2018 Ulysse Allard; 2019 Sophie Parent; 2020-2021 not awarded (COVID-19); 2022 Miriam Vandervort Charboneau; 2023 Simon MacLaren; 2024 Margot Simonian; 2025 Laurent Thuot; 2026 Charlie MacLaren.
Five Order of Owens seasons had two recipients each (1984, 1996, 1998, 2004, 2012), giving 54 individual recipients across 49 award seasons.

The Order of Owens was not awarded in either 2020 or 2021, independently corroborating from a camp-internal award record that Camp Kanawana's overnight camp was closed for both consecutive seasons -- consistent with Sean Day's documented 2021 decision to keep the overnight camp closed for a second season and pivot to 10 day camps.

The Order of Owens roster is kept on carved wooden award paddles at Camp Kanawana. Two are documented: an older paddle lettered in blackletter running 2005-2012, and a later cursive paddle running 2005-2022. Both begin at 2005, so neither covers the 1976-2004 portion of the roster.

The cursive Order of Owens paddle runs directly from '2019 - Sophie Parent' to '2022 - Miriam Vandervort Charboneau', confirming the two-season 2020-2021 COVID gap on the physical artifact rather than only in operator account.

Two unresolved spelling discrepancies exist between the Order of Owens paddles and the operator-supplied roster: the 2008 recipient appears as 'Oscar Newsam' on the paddles against 'Oskar Newsam' in the roster; and the 2009 recipient appears as 'Russell Donahue' on the blackletter paddle but 'Russel Donahue' on the cursive paddle and in the roster -- the 2009 case being an inconsistency between the two artifacts themselves.

Camp Kanawana holds a perpetual trophy for the L&V Games, wall-mounted as a crossed paddle and axe over a red backing with a central shield reading 'KANAWANA ANNUAL TROPHY for LUMBERMEN VOYAGEUR GAMES'. Rows of shield plaques beneath record the winning team for each season, running from 47 (1947) to 25 (2025) in two-digit years, alternating irregularly between Voyageurs and Lumbermen, with the singular 'Lumberman' used on several late-1970s entries.

The L&V Games annual trophy's shields have NOT been reliably transcribed: the available photographs are angled, several plaques sit behind the crossed paddle and axe, and older shields are faded or silvered. A careful read would yield a near-complete 79-season winners roll and settle which season was skipped, which currently rests on arithmetic from YMCA Quebec's '78th edition' claim for 2025.

The charter of the Order of the Knights of Kanawana proclaims the order 'in this Year of Our Lord Nineteen Hundred and Eighty', establishing 'a select group of Kanawanians who upon proving themselves worthy, will then become Ladies and Knights of the Land', to be 'challenged Aquatically and Terrestrially, Morally and Intellectually', judged by a council only after all challenges are met, invested 'in a secret ceremony, at the discretion of the council', and thereafter retaining 'their positions of honour forever'.

The Knights of Kanawana charter sets out six challenges for knighthood: (1) participate in at least two five-day canoe trips, displaying leadership in trip preparation, en route and in camp; (2) achieve one A and one B in kampcraft and canoeing plus C-level standing in other approved areas including sailing, orienteering, archery and rock climbing; (3) complete a distance swim of at least two miles; (4) assist teaching an interest group throughout an entire session; (5) contribute something of permanence to camp, the charter's examples being 'a substantial part of a totem pole, or a bridge'; (6) learn to identify six different trees and three edible plants.

L&V Games winners transcribed from the Annual Trophy, 1947-1975: 1947 Voyageurs; 1948 Voyageurs; 1949 illegible; 1950 Lumbermen; 1951 Lumbermen; 1952 year visible but team illegible; 1953 Lumbermen; 1954 Lumbermen; 1955 Lumbermen; 1956 Voyageurs; 1957 Voyageurs; 1958 illegible; 1959 Voyageurs; 1960 Voyageurs; 1961 illegible; 1962 Voyageurs; 1963 Voyageurs; 1964 Lumbermen; 1965 Lumbermen; 1966 Lumbermen; 1967 Voyageurs; 1968 Lumbermen; 1969 Lumbermen; 1970 Lumbermen; 1971 Lumbermen; 1972 Voyageurs; 1973 Lumbermen; 1974 Voyageurs; 1975 Lumbermen.

L&V Games winners transcribed from the Annual Trophy, 1976-2025: 1976 Lumberman; 1977 Lumberman; 1978 Lumberman; 1979 Voyageurs; 1980 Voyageurs; 1981 Voyageurs; 1982 Voyageurs; 1983 Lumbermen; 1984 Lumbermen; 1985 Voyageurs; 1986 Lumbermen; 1987 Lumbermen; 1988 Voyageurs; 1989 Voyageurs; 1990 Lumbermen; 1991 Lumbermen; 1992 Voyageurs; 1993 Voyageurs; 1994 Voyageurs; 1995 Voyageurs; 1996 Lumbermen; 1997 Voyageurs; 1998 Voyageurs; 1999 Lumbermen; 2000 Voyageurs; 2001 Lumbermen; 2002 Voyageurs; 2003 Lumbermen; 2004 Voyageurs; 2005 Lumbermen; 2006 Voyageurs; 2007 Lumbermen; 2008 Lumbermen; 2009 Lumbermen; 2010 Voyageurs; 2011 Voyageurs; 2012 Lumbermen; 2013 Voyageurs; 2014 Voyageurs; 2015 Lumbermen; 2016 Lumbermen; 2017 Voyageurs; 2018 Voyageurs; 2019 Lumbermen; 2020 Voyageurs; 2021 NO SHIELD FOUND; 2022 Lumbermen; 2023 Lumbermen; 2024 Lumbermen; 2025 Voyageurs. Years 1976-1978 are lettered in the singular 'Lumberman'.

Across the 74 legible seasons on the L&V Annual Trophy, the Lumbermen won 38 and the Voyageurs 36. The longest legible consecutive runs are four seasons: Lumbermen 1975-1978 and 2022-2024 (three), and Voyageurs 1992-1995.

A plaque mounted above the L&V Annual Trophy reads 'KANAWANA STAMPEDE / 1976 CHAMPIONS', with further lettering not legible in the available photograph. The 'Kanawana Stampede' appears nowhere else in this project's wiki, KB or sources -- an entirely undocumented camp event or competition.

The Knights of Kanawana charter's second challenge shows the camp operating a lettered A/B/C skill-grading system across named activity areas -- kampcraft, canoeing, sailing, orienteering, archery and rock climbing are named -- requiring one A and one B in kampcraft and canoeing plus C-level standing elsewhere. Part of the clause, including an apparent ball-game activity name and an equivalence notation, is illegible in the available photograph.

The Knights of Kanawana charter spells the camp 'Kamp' in its fifth challenge ('contribute something of permanence to Kamp'), consistent with the K-spelling being the camp's own usage in 1980-81 and with the documented transition to 'Camp' in spring 2005.

The Knights of Kanawana charter is a birchbark sheet: a painted black lake-and-island scene with conifers and a lone standing dead tree fills the upper half, pressed maple and fern leaves run down both margins, the proclamation and six challenges are hand-lettered in two columns below, and a drawn log carrying further lettering closes the foot, signed and dated 1981.

The 2020 L&V Games were played remotely during the first COVID-19 summer: volunteer alumni and campers competed in individual and online challenges from within their socially-distanced 'bubbles'. The Voyageurs won, and a 2020 shield appears on the Annual Trophy.

The 2021 L&V Games were not held. 2021 is therefore the only season since the Games' 1947 founding in which they were not contested, which reconciles YMCA Quebec's description of 2025 as the 78th edition (79 seasons from 1947 to 2025, minus one).

The Order of Owens was not awarded in either 2020 or 2021 while the L&V Games were contested in 2020, because the two honours measure different things: the Games could be abstracted into individual and online challenges, whereas the Order of Owens recognises canoe-tripping leadership that cannot be earned without an in-person camp.

Three L&V Games winners not legible in the trophy photographs were supplied directly: 1949 Lumbermen, 1952 Voyageurs, 1958 Lumbermen. The 1961 winner remains unknown and is to be verified against the trophy itself.

The 2026 L&V Games were won by the Lumbermen, decided on the night of 14 August 2026. As the 79th edition (79 contested seasons since 1947, 2021 excepted), the result was not yet on the Annual Trophy when it was photographed earlier that day.

Across the 78 known L&V Games seasons of 79 contested between 1947 and 2026, the Lumbermen have won 41 and the Voyageurs 37. The longest run by either team is four consecutive seasons, achieved four times: Lumbermen 1968-1971 and 1975-1978, Voyageurs 1979-1982 and 1992-1995.

The single unknown L&V season, 1961, sits between Voyageur wins in 1959-1960 and 1962-1963. If 1961 was a Voyageur year it would form a five-season run (1959-1963), longer than any other run on the trophy; if a Lumbermen year, it separates two ordinary pairs. The one unread shield therefore determines whether the longest run in the Games' history exists.

Operator recollection holds that the 1961 L&V Games went to the Voyageurs, inferred from the Voyageurs being remembered as holding the longest unbroken run. This is UNCONFIRMED and abductive: a Voyageur record run requires five consecutive seasons, which only 1961 can supply, so the reasoning infers the shield from the remembered run rather than recalling the shield itself. It cannot serve as independent confirmation of the run it would create. 1961 remains marked unknown pending a read of the trophy.

Two components of the same operator recollection are independently confirmed by the transcribed winners roll: the Lumbermen hold slightly more wins overall (41-37), and the gap narrowed sharply during the operator's camper years -- between 1991 and 1998 the Voyageurs took six of eight seasons, cutting the Lumbermen's lead from +6 to +1, the sharpest sustained swing in the record.

The L&V series has swung considerably despite its near-even final tally. The Voyageurs led the all-time series only in its first two seasons (1947-1948). The Lumbermen built to a high-water mark of +7 by 1978, having won 19 of the first 31 seasons. The Voyageurs then took 11 of 17 seasons between 1979 and 1995, cutting the deficit to two and by 1998 to one. The series remained within one or two wins for two decades before the Lumbermen widened it back to +4 by 2026.
